extracted.intended_audience: actors, acting students, improvisation teachers, and performers interested in Viola Spolin's theatre games
extracted.subtask_description: Practical guidance on teaching and practicing Viola Spolin's theater games to develop present-moment focus, physical expressiveness, ensemble listening, and spontaneous creativity. Includes descriptions and purposes of specific games (Contact, Gibberish, Mirror Speech).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritize what students are doing on stage (action over lines)
rubrics_metrics.description: Spolin prioritized what the students were doing on stage, rather than on the lines they were saying.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus exercises on actors' actions and interactions instead of memorized dialogue; design activities that emphasize doing, movement and choices rather than scripted text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use open-ended, cooperative games and avoid prescribing 'how' to do things
rubrics_metrics.description: Using open-ended, cooperative games, she never would tell students how to do something. Whatever creative choice a student made was never 'right' or 'wrong.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt non-directive facilitation—provide constraints or prompts but do not demonstrate or correct exact choices; encourage experimentation and multiple possible solutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cultivate present-moment focus and intuition (body, mind, intuition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Help actors focus on the present moment and make creative choices through improvisation; 'you’re getting it into the body—body, mind, intuition.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design exercises that pull participants out of overthinking and into embodied, immediate responses; reward spontaneous, intuitive reactions rather than preplanned ones.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diminish self-consciousness to unleash creativity and natural acting
rubrics_metrics.description: The games were designed to take the emphasis off of 'acting,' diminish their self-consciousness, unleash their creativity, and allow them to act more naturally on stage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use playful, non-evaluative games that reduce performers' fear of judgment and encourage risk-taking and authenticity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use games to break down barriers and build ensemble bonding
rubrics_metrics.description: Spolin could see the games breaking down barriers and bonding people closer together; mirror games produced 'a feeling of oneness.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select activities that require interdependence and shared focus to develop trust, connection, and ensemble cohesion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contact game: speech only during physical contact; invent new contact each time
rubrics_metrics.description: Actors may only speak when making physical contact with a scene partner, and they must continue to invent and initiate a new way of touching each time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the Contact constraint to force physical expression and variety; continually change permitted contact methods (e.g., no more hands) to push creativity and prevent habitual choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gibberish: improvise in a made-up language with interpreters to provide context
rubrics_metrics.description: Two performers improvise a conversation in a made-up language, while a third, and sometimes a fourth, actor interprets their words, giving context about the story for the audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ gibberish-plus-interpreter exercises to focus on emotional and physical clarity, create bonds between performers and audience, and practice conveying meaning without relying on literal language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mirror Speech: exact mirroring to cultivate focus and unity; switch roles smoothly
rubrics_metrics.description: Two people, one the initiator and the other the mirror, stand face-to-face. The mirror exactly copies the words and movements of the initiator; then they 'switch' roles, continuing momentum.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use mirroring to develop intense partner listening, timing, and ensemble responsiveness; practice seamless role-switching to maintain flow and shared momentum.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apply continuous novel constraints to increase creativity
rubrics_metrics.description: Spolin would say, 'No more hands, find a different way to make contact and incorporate it into the scene,' continuously restricting their contact options to increase creativity and intuition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Introduce evolving restrictions within games (forbid habitual solutions) so performers must generate fresh, creative responses under changing conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value internal transformation over producing a 'perfect' product
rubrics_metrics.description: Spolin: 'I think that the creative act must transform the one who is in it—not what he produces but what happens to him or her?'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess success by performers’ growth in presence, confidence, and responsiveness rather than by polished outcomes; prioritize learning and personal change.
